meta.financial_picture: Frontline was bought by Broad Sky on Dec 9, 2024 through BSP-FL Holdings Inc. The deal was funded by an equity vehicle (BSP-FL LP) that sold $136.95M to 21 investors, plus a $90M initial term loan co-led by NXT Capital and Audax Private Debt (UK sub accounts, note 11). Carlyle AlpInvest separately put $12.5M of equity directly into BSP-FL Intermediate Inc. on Dec 5, 2024, and BV Investment Partners rolled a minority stake. Sponsor equity is therefore roughly $137-150M plus rollover, against $90M of debt, or about 60% equity. Adding equity and debt gives a transaction value of roughly $230-260M. If the lenders sized the $90M loan at a typical 4.5-5.5x LMM leverage, adjusted EBITDA at close was about $16-20M, for an entry multiple of about 12-15x. The BV-era debt history supports that range. Webster Bank lent $30M plus a $5M revolver in Feb 2019, and term debt reached $47.7M by Dec 2023 after the 2020-21 add-ons. At bank-style 3-4x leverage, that implies 2023 EBITDA of about $12-16M, growing into the $16-20M implied at the BSP close. Headcount rose from 600+ (2020, after Hilltop) to about 850 (c.2022), 1,000+ (2023) and about 1,100 (Jan 2026), with a heavy offshore base (Goa, Hyderabad, Cape Town). At an assumed $90-130K revenue per employee for an offshore-weighted legal MSP/BPO, revenue is estimated at about $100-140M, implying 13-18% EBITDA margins. The MSP 501 ranks (#38 in 2024, #36 in 2026) weight revenue, EBITDA and recurring revenue, which supports a large-MSP scale ($100M+) without giving an exact band. After the close, Carlyle held the position at cost for five quarters, then marked it up about 10% to $13.75M at 3/31/2026, a modest positive signal after the Jan 2026 CEO change to Tim Britt (ex-Synoptek roll-up founder). Relative to rivals, Frontline's structure is simpler and cheaper than Elevate's (about 12.8%+ venture debt), less stretched than Consilio's (senior plus PIK sub debt), and healthier-looking than Epiq's (loan marked about 91% of par). Frontline's own loan pricing is not public, but Audax's comparable LMM unitranches (for example Mitratech at S+475) suggest roughly S+475-550. Main open risks: undisclosed incremental debt for a likely buy-and-build (KL Software, Aug 2026), UK sub filing lapses, and inconsistent client-count disclosures.
